crime: When {WITCH_NAME} was small, she once spoke up in her father's classroom. He was the headmaster. The class fell silent for her, then turned back to one another.
In the prison, another prisoner recorded a picture book in the library every evening for the girls who couldn't sleep. {WITCH_NAME} read the fox, and the reader answered as the rabbit.
During free time one evening, the reader took the fox's lines back and began recording both parts herself. "When you read," she said, "the hall hears only you."

At "And the fox said," {WITCH_NAME} stopped the recording. She closed both hands around the reader's throat and held on until the girl went still. Then she played the clip from the start, set the phone by the reader's hand, left the door open, and stepped out to the upper railing before the others came up.

As they did every night after their showers, the prisoners gathered at the railing and listened to the recorded reading through the open door. When it reached the cut, {WITCH_NAME} began to speak. Her Magic hushed the second-floor hall, every head turned toward her, and the reading fell silent with it. When she finished, they turned back to one another and went downstairs talking before lockup, with her among them.

At trial, the prisoners accused the reader's roommate, who had gone up and found her. The reader, they said, had still been alive when that speech began, silenced by its first word like everyone else, and had been killed after it ended.
Then a prisoner played the last clip on the reader's phone. It ended on "And the fox said." No hush followed, and no voice.
The prisoners understood: a girl held silent by the Magic could not have stopped her own recording. The reader was already dead when {WITCH_NAME} began speaking where the clip cut off.
fields.epitaph: The only voice that ever answered her was the one she stopped.
fields.epithet: The Headmaster's Daughter No One Answered
execution: The execution stand raised a giant iron hourglass. She hung chained upright in its lower bulb.
Iron sand began to pour onto her head. She spoke to make it stop. The trial court fell silent and listened to her, and the sand poured on.
It rose past her chest, then to her mouth, her lips still moving.
The last grain fell onto a full bulb. The spectators turned back to one another and talked.

magic.name: All Ears
magic.text: When she speaks, everyone within earshot falls silent and listens only to her until she stops.
